label: PF Backlog 575
title: One-step add: groom the item at create (epic auto-assign, dependencies, execution order) instead of a separate later step
body:
## Problem / why
Adding a backlog item and grooming it are two logical steps today. On create only a deterministic
analysis runs (PFSSOT-P3, core/backlog.py:838-842); epic assignment happens only for some automated
creators (core/intake.py:164, core/issues.py:244, core/insights.py:140, core/intake_channels.py:331,
core/ops_phase.py:99 via auto_epic), a direct add leaves epic='' (warning core/backlog.py:843-845),
structured dependencies come only from explicit deps (core/grooming.py:191-198), and the epic execution
order is computed later by the scheduler (core/scheduler.py:550-578). Items are therefore not
scheduler-ready on creation.

## Goal
On the FIRST add, run the SAME grooming the standard path runs (AI + deterministic, batch-capable) and
complete planning: auto-assign the epic (best match else Unscoped), populate dependencies, and persist
the epic execution order - so add is one step and the item is scheduler-ready.

## In scope
- core/backlog.py add_epic (single create path): if no epic passed and the item is not an epic, auto_epic(...).
- Call the SAME grooming routine as elsewhere (default mode: AI with deterministic fallback), not a
  deterministic-only variant.
- After the epic is known, derive and persist the epic execution order (core.scheduler.epic_order ->
  backlog.set_execution_order).
- First-time-only guard: stamp the item so re-adds (same external_id) and updates do not re-groom.

## Out of scope
- Inferring dependencies from related items (explicit deps/blocked_by only).
- Changing the grooming engine or the AI prompt.

## Approach
Move the epic-assign + groom + order steps into add_epic after the item is written and the lock released
(as today), guarded by a groomed marker; amend the PFSSOT-P3 decision (on-entry = full groom, not
deterministic-only).

## Acceptance criteria
- Adding an item with no epic attaches it to the best-match epic, else Unscoped (no epic-less item from a plain add).
- The on-add analysis matches the standard grooming output (same routine).
- The epic's execution_order is persisted after add.
- Re-adding the same external_id and updating an item do not re-groom (first-time only).
- Tests cover the above; precheck passes.

## Risks
- A create may block on a live AI call; mitigate with the existing deterministic fallback (never blocks)
  and first-time-only scoping.

## Rollback
Revert the add_epic change; items still groom via the later pass (groom_all/refresh_stale).
